packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-13 — unverified image reading

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading. Blind reading. I have not tried to identify work or author.

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Observations
- Two faces of one narrow vertical parchment strip, about 7.5 cm wide by 16.5 cm tall (ruler in frame). image-001 is the overview and image-002 the native tile of one face (here "face 1"); image-003 overview and image-004 tile of the other ("face 2").
- Text upright on both faces. 13 lines on each face in the upper half of the strip; the lower half is blank on both faces, so the text ends above a deep lower margin (or the bottom of a column).
- A long vertical tear/loss runs down the middle from about line 3 to below the text, removing two to four letters from each of lines 4-13 on both faces. A horizontal fold or join crosses the strip at about line 5.
- Face 1: the left edge is cut through the writing (first letters of every line lost); the right edge appears to be the true line end (hyphen strokes at ends of lines 6, 10, 12). Face 2: the left edge is the true line start with a small margin; the right edge is cut through the writing (line ends lost). So a single column, trimmed on one vertical side.
- Script: a small formal book hand (gothic textualis type) in dark brown ink, heavily abbreviated. Red paragraph marks (paraph signs) on face 1 lines 1 and 9 and face 2 lines 3, 6 and 11; one red-touched capital "E" on face 1 line 5. No running title, rubric heading, enlarged initial or underlining. A few small interlinear additions in the same or a similar hand (face 1 lines 2-3 above the line; face 2 line 1 "-us" above, line 3 superscript, line 8 "lo" above "ca").
- Modern pencil note on the blank lower part of face 1: "VIII B 20/157".

Tentative interpretation
- Short units introduced by paraph + "Item debemus …", each followed by scriptural allegations with book abbreviations and chapter numerals ("ecc.", "Ie. iiii", "xxiiii", "x. ca(pitu)lo"), and by "i." (id est) glossing: this looks like a distinctio- or sermon-type development on preparing the heart, not a text with separate commentary. No lemma/commentary hierarchy is visible in this narrow strip. Which face is recto is not shown by the images.

2. SPANS SELECTED / UNREAD
All 13 lines of each face transcribed. Nothing left unread except letters physically lost at the cut edge and in the central tear. A wider view cannot be had from this strip; an adjacent strip from the same leaf would be needed to complete the lines.

3. TRANSCRIPTION
Conventions: ( ) = my expansion of an abbreviation; [lost] = parchment missing (cut edge or central tear); ¶ = red paraph; ? after a reading = uncertain. Letters in [ ] followed by ? are a suggestion for a partly visible word, not a supply from any source.

FACE 1 — image-002 (lines from top of image-002; image-001 is the overview of the same face). Left edge cut.

image-002 L1:  [lost]ne bonor(um) op(er)um. ¶ Et seq(ui)tur q(ui)
image-002 L2:  [lost]ate erant. gl(os)a? [small interlinear mark above] quib(us) (con)sci(enti)a bona
image-002 L3:  [lost]iu(m)? testi(moniu)m dabat. iii?. sic. q(ui) p(re)p(ar)ate
image-002 L4:  [lost]nt. i. q(ui) p(re)p(ar)a[lost]nt. vasa sua. i.
image-002 L5:  [lost]da sua inv[lost]nt ecc(…). Et ip(s)e
image-002 L6:  [lost] p(re)p(ar)at(i)o(ne)m co[lost] eor(um) audivit au-
image-002 L7:  [lost]s tua (et)c. ecc[lost]. q(ui) timent d(omi)n(u)m
image-002 L8:  [lost]abu(n)t corda [lost]a (et) i(n) (con)spectu ip(s)i(us)
image-002 L9:  [lost]ficabu(n)t a(n)i(m)a[lost]uas. ¶ Item debe(mus)
image-002 L10: [lost]are corda n[lost]ra sic(ut) hospes hos-
image-002 L11: [lost]ciu(m) suu(m) pa[lost]s (con)tra? aliq(ue)m magnu(m)
image-002 L12: [lost]e hac p(re)p(ar)at(i)o(n)e [lost]i?. xxiiii. p(re)para fo-
image-002 L13: [lost]s opus tuu(m) (et) [lost]exerce agru(m) tuum

Notes face 1:
- L2 "gl(os)a?": written "gl" with a superscript letter and abbreviation stroke; could also be "g(e)n(er)o" or similar. A tiny interlinear sign stands just below the end of L1 at this point.
- L3: the numeral after "dabat." is three or four minims with a superscript stroke ("iii" / "iiii" / possibly "u(er)"), followed by "sic."; I cannot decide.
- L5: a black horizontal stroke at the left under "[..]da" looks like a tear edge or later mark, not a deletion. "E" of "Et" is touched with red.
- L7 "ecc[lost]": the book abbreviation is broken by the tear; one or two characters (perhaps a chapter numeral) lost.
- L11: the sign after "pa[lost]s" is a 9-shaped "con" with superscript "a" — "(con)tra" most likely.
- L13: before "exerce" a stroke that may be the end of an adverb or "dilig(en)t(er)"-type abbreviation; only the last minim survives.

FACE 2 — image-004 (lines from top of image-004; image-003 is the overview of the same face). Right edge cut.

image-004 L1:  q(ui) d(ebe)t induere se v[lost]ti[b](us)? [interlinear "-us"/"9" above] regalib(us) h[lost]
image-004 L2:  bonis v(ir)tutib(us) u[lost] placeat reg[lost]
image-004 L3:  suero. i. (Christ)o q(ui)? b[lost] imp(er)e(…)? [superscript letters above, "ra"/"rau"?] ¶ Ite(m) [lost]
image-004 L4:  bem(us) corda nost[lost]rare ad su[lost]
image-004 L5:  piend(um) sic(ut) vas [lost] [two or three words crushed in the fold: "…u(m)? ad aliq(ue)m?" very uncertain] [lost]
image-004 L6:  quore(m) gr(ati)e est? [lost] eor(um). ¶ p(ri)mo [lost]
image-004 L7:  lavari p(er) (con)fessio[lost] sicut h(abetu)r. Ie(…). iiii. [lost]
image-004 L8:  va a malicia co[lost] tuu(m). (et) x. ca(pitu)lo ["lo" written above] [lost]
image-004 L9:  d(icitu)r d(e)b(e)t? q(uod) lavit se [lost] unxit cor(pus) su[lost]
image-004 L10: mirra optima [lost] salutaria? p(e)n(itenti)[lost]
image-004 L11: ¶ Iud(i)t(h) (con)fitens (et) [lost]stificans int(er)p(re)[lost]
image-004 L12: (et) sig(nifica)t a(n)i(m)am fide[lost]m q(ue) d(ebe)t lavari [lost]
image-004 L13: (con)fessione(m). (et) d(e)m[lost] om(n)ib(us) op(er)ib(us) su[lost]

Notes face 2:
- L1-L3 run on as one sentence: "… q(ui) debet induere se v[..]tib(us) regalib(us) h[..] / bonis virtutibus u[t] placeat reg[..] / suero. i. Christo …" — "suero" at the start of L3 is the end of a word begun at the lost end of L2.
- L3: after "(Christ)o" the reading is damaged by the head of the tear; "q(ui)" with superscript, "b…", then "imp(er)e…" with letters added above the line. I cannot read the phrase securely.
- L4 "bem(us)" continues a word begun at the lost end of L3 (after "Ite(m)"); L5 "piend(um)" continues from the lost end of L4; L6 "quore(m)" continues from the lost end of L5; L8 "va" continues from the lost end of L7.
- L7 "Ie." is "I" + "e" with a stroke, followed by chapter numeral "iiii"; the next line gives "x. ca(pitu)lo" for a second reference whose book name is lost at the line end.
- L9: "d(icitu)r" followed by "dz" with stroke and "q" with stroke; expansions "d(e)b(e)t" / "de" + name are both possible; I leave it open.
- L10: "salutaria" may be "(et) salutaria" or part of a longer word; the first letters are in the tear.
- L11: red paraph precedes "Iud(i)t(h)"; the name is written "Jud" with superscript "t".

4. LIMITATIONS
- Every line lacks letters at one cut edge and in the central tear; no line is complete, so lines do not join without loss.
- Face order (recto/verso) and how much text is missing between the faces cannot be told from the images.
- Chapter numerals and the book abbreviations "ecc." are read as seen; I have not checked them against any text.
- This is an unverified image reading.

Reader activity: opened PROMPT.md; image-001.jpg, image-002.jpg, image-003.jpg, image-004.jpg. (READER.md and the directory listing were opened earlier in this session; packet.json not opened.)
